uncited: Computes the distance along a ray direction from a given point to the nearest intersection with an axis-aligned bounding box (AABB).
It returns -1 if the starting point is inside the box or if the ray does not intersect the box.

It differs from standard intersection tests by returning a scalar distance value rather than a boolean or hit point, which is useful for sorting or early-out optimizations in volume rendering pipelines.
Returns -1 if no valid intersection exists (point inside or ray misses).
- Vectors are treated as 3-element arrays or tuples $(x, y, z)$.
Normalize the ray direction vector $\vec{d}$ to unit length.
Let $v$ be the coordinate of `point` on axis $i$.
Let $d$ be the component of `direction` on axis $i$.
Let $min_i$ and $max_i$ be the minimum and maximum extents of the AABB on axis $i$.
- If $v < min_i$ and $d > 0$: Set `dist` = $(min_i - v) / d$.
- If $v > max_i$ and $d < 0$: Set `dist` = $(max_i - v) / d$.
- If $v < min_i$ and $d > 0$: Set `dist` = $\max(\text{dist}, (min_i - v) / d)$.
- If $v > max_i$ and $d < 0$: Set `dist` = $\max(\text{dist}, (max_i - v) / d)$.
